title: Pairing message, pairing-message/1 (DEC-0084)
description: One message of the pairing that adds a machine to an estate (DEC-0084, docs/specification/ceremonies.md): a side's commitment, its reveal, or an abort. Both sides commit before either reveals; the commitment is SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 form of {type: fabric-enroll-commit/1, role, keys, nonce}, with genesis for the trusted side (pairingCommit); the comparison code both screens show is derived from both reveals (comparisonCode). A one-time relay rendezvous (relay.md) or a local connection carries these messages and nothing else.

commit.description: sha256: and the hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 RFC 8785 form of {type: fabric-enroll-commit/1, role, keys, nonce}: the side's keys and nonce, hidden until its reveal.

keys.description: The side's device keys as an estate record lists them (DEC-0053, FAC-SEM-073): exactly one <id>#sig and at most one <id>#kem, for one machine id. The new machine's are the keys the revision that adds it lists; the trusted machine's #sig is the one the current revision lists for it.

oneOf.description: The new machine's reveal: its keys and nonce. It names no estate: it has none yet.

The new machine's are the keys the revision that adds it lists; the trusted machine's #sig is the one the current revision lists for it.

genesis.description: The digest of revision 1 of the trusted machine's estate. The commitment and the comparison code cover it, so the code binds the network too, and the new machine pins revision 1 only when its digest is this one (joinListed).

oneOf.description: The trusted machine's reveal: its keys, its nonce and its estate's genesis.
Either side ends the rendezvous: a reveal that does not open its commitment, or the person said the codes differ. It burns the rendezvous; a new attempt opens a new one with new nonces.

role.description: new: the machine that joins (or re-pairs under its id to replace its key); trusted: a machine of the estate on which the person signs the next revision.

nonce.description: 32 fresh random bytes, unpadded base64url; never reused across rendezvous.
